verdict.rationale: Parahelp's own Automations feature runs Internal Agent tasks on event triggers such as a GitHub PR merging, and an Automations page offers templates. Natural-language guardrail rules like routing enterprise tickets also act on ticket events, and actions can be set to auto-approve per task or automation. The catalog of trigger events, the rule-definition semantics, and the trigger configuration are thinly documented (one example trigger), and actions require manual approval by default. missing for 10: a documented list of supported trigger events and how they are configured, explicit rule syntax and conditions for trigger-to-action mappings, and independent or hands-on corroboration that triggered automations run end-to-end without manual steps.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: An automation is an Internal Agent task that runs on a schedule, like every weekday at 9am, or a trigger, like a GitHub PR merging
Set up automations on the "Automations" page. It shows all existing automations and includes templates for common setups.
When a ticket is about an enterprise account, transfer it to the enterprise team with a summary note.
Enable auto-approve for a task or automation, and the Internal Agent can perform any action through the connection without asking for approval.
By default, every action requires manual approval. You can set specific tools to auto-approve per task or automation
